name: The Chi of Yore
description: It seems Mt. Qingce is hiding some secrets...

steps.description: Ask the locals of Qingce Village about the fragments
Ask Granny Ruoxin about the fragments
Find a way into the vault
Head to Qingce Village and report to Granny Ruoxin
Head to the ruin to search for fragments
Go to the highest point of Qingce Village to search for fragments.
Search for fragments near the Geo Statues
Head to Qingce Village and ask the village chief about the situation.
Head to Qingce Village and ask the locals about the fragments

dialogs.content: "...studies show that these ruins date back to very ancient times indeed; they are older than the collective age of all the elderly residents of Qingce Village put together."
"In other words, we find these ruins to be entirely generic, indistinguishable in substance from other ruins."

"Yet despite their generic nature, the majority of these ruins contain treasure. Though driven out by the Ruin Hunters here, the allure of the treasure contained within will be sure to see the Treasure Hoarders return."

"According to Chang the Ninth, who lives on the mountain, there was once an old town below. Once it was destroyed there was... what was it... something that was sealed away underground. Something to do with some kind of golden stone..."

"But he's a destitute scholar who loves citing the classics and going off on tangents. Added to the fact that I drank a lot with him to get the conversation going, I can't remember what he said very clearly. I think the crux of it was that it had something to do with some golden stone and Ruin Hunters... That old man really can drink a lot."
"The heavy drinking and the bitterly cold wind have left my head feeling like it's been bashed about by a bunch of hilichurls."

"Actually now I think about it... Maybe I really did get attacked by hilichurls on my way down the mountain last night? I can't remember for sure... My head sure does hurt though. Better get myself to a doctor in Liyue Harbor before thinking any more about these ruins."
"With the evil serpent gone from Qingce, the magic formula that subdued it was no longer in effect. ..."
"...But the serpent did not perish, and its foul blood congealed within the earth and formed stone, poisoning the world..."
"...Thus three statues were used to subdue it..."
...Just three lines and Paimon's head is hurting. Why are all Liyue's stories written like this?
But anyway, that bit that goes <color=#00E1FFFF>"foul blood something something formed stone"</color>... does that mean there's <color=#00E1FFFF>strange stone</color> around here?
Let's take a look around at the <color=#00E1FFFF>stones</color> around here and see if we can find some leads.

"...Rex Lapis overcame the Chi, but the Chi could not perish in its entirety. Thus did Rex Lapis conquer each of its facets in turn: its spirit was bound in the <color=#00E1FFFF>north</color>, its bones were pinned in the <color=#00E1FFFF>south-east</color>, its flesh was incarcerated in the <color=#00E1FFFF>north-west</color>, its soul was fettered in the <color=#00E1FFFF>north-east</color>, and its form was crushed in the <color=#00E1FFFF>south-west</color>..."
"...Its bones pierced, its spirit faded, its form and soul both decimated... still did its flesh survive..."

Here stands this statue, to <color=#00E1FFFF>watch in each direction</color>: the <color=#00E1FFFF>wind-swept ruin</color>, the <color=#00E1FFFF>snow-capped peak</color>, the <color=#00E1FFFF>adepti's abode</color>, and the <color=#00E1FFFF>city of Liyue</color>...
Agh, what terrible luck...
What happened?
Oh, Traveler. You've come at the right time. I was just doing some, uh, research.
You know the name of this place, right? Qingce Village?
So, how do I say this... Do you understand what "Qingce" means?
Understand... what?
Well, its origin and hidden meaning, of course. Should have known you weren't the cultured sort...
Do you know about the Chi? According to legend, the Chi was a dragon-like monster that once forcibly occupied this place.
When Rex Lapis — or Morax — defeated it, the Chi's body twisted into rock, its blood turned into water, and its scales became the terraced fields.
And in times long past, the word "Chi" also used to mean "Qingce."
And, through my long, earnest and rigorous research...
I believe that the Chi's corpse may still be on this mountain.
That logic didn't add up...
Hmph, don't be so dismissive. Haven't you noticed the giant trees growing in this area? Don't you think that they're a lot larger and sturdier than elsewhere?
The locals call these Blood-Fed Trees. They believe that these trees grew by absorbing the Chi's blood, and that the area where they grew are the Chi's Eyes.
And indeed, the growth of these trees is abnormal.
Even if it were not truly the corpse of that monster, there must be something incredible underground...
Of course! How could I give up on something so... researchable?
I say that, but the truth is that I don't have a lot of leads.
It is, after all, an antediluvian legend. It's likely that barely anyone even remembers the legend anymore.
After all the effort I put into finding these ruins, thinking that I might be able to find something in here...
...It turned out that there's a <color=#00E1FFFF>Ruin Hunter</color> standing guard inside. That's why I said that my luck was terrible.
I'd really like to go in and have a look, but it's far too dangerous. I'll probably wait until it leaves before giving this a go.
Are you looking to go inside and explore, by any chance? Not that I'd stop you, no, but...
Please be mindful of your safety. This might be the clue to some treasure, but it's just a legend in the end. Don't pay it too much mind.
And what would the corpse be used for?
Uses? For a monster's corpse? Do you even have any idea...
Ahem! Do you even know how valuable it is for research?
This is your research?
It's pretty unique.
That's it? "It's pretty unique"? So uncultured...
This way, I can... Whoa! Y—You're still here?
I'm going to rest for a while, and then... then I'll be going.
Take care of yourself now, and don't push yourself too much. For all we know, it really is just a legend.
I have this fragment...
A fragment of...? Found something curious, have you? Let me see...
Heh... No wonder you can't make head or tail of it. This isn't writing on here — it's a drawing.
Long, long ago, before writing was invented, people recorded events with pictures.
Look, this symbol here depicts the Chi — a legendary beast. It looks like the full symbol must have been very large and complex, this is only part of it. But it's enough for me to recognize it by.
My guess is that this depicts the battle between the Geo Lord and the Chi. But it's hard to be more specific from just this one piece.
If you had all the pieces, could you make sense of it?
Oh, I don't know about that. No guarantee.
But what I can guarantee is that without all the pieces, I certainly can't make sense of it.
Watch me, I'll find the rest in no time.
Hehe... So much enthusiasm. I like that about young people.
Given what this fragment is showing, I'd say that if you really want to find the other fragments, here's what you should do...
According to the legend of the Geo Lord and the Chi, the battle took place at a <color=#00E1FFFF>great height</color>. So you could try your luck on the mountaintops around here.
Beyond that, there are many traces of the battle in this area. <color=#00E1FFFF>Ruins</color> would be a sensible place to look.

In every conflict there is a losing side. The legend tells that after defeating the Chi, the Geo Lord instructed our forebears to erect <color=#00E1FFFF>Geo Statues</color> to crush the Chi's remaining power.
I'd guess you would have a higher chance of finding things to do with the Chi in places with lots of <color=#00E1FFFF>Geo Statues</color>.

For example, there are many <color=#00E1FFFF>Geo Statues</color> erected <color=#00E1FFFF>west</color> of Qingce Village. It's said that's the very spot where the Geo Lord crushed the Chi... Maybe you'll strike lucky over that way.
Once you've found all the fragments, bring them to me. I'll be waiting right here.
I have some fragments...
Let's see now... Why, these fragments all fit together.
See here, this is the symbol for a Chi, and this Chi was defeated in a major battle.
Afterward, it was pinned down in a deep place.
What's a Chi?
In the legends, the Chi was a dragon-like monster, and Mt. Qingce was once its lair.
When Rex Lapis — or Morax — defeated it, the Chi's body twisted into rock, its blood turned into water, and its scales became the terraced fields.
Do you see those sturdy trees near Qingce Village? Those are Blood-Fed Trees, said to have been nourished by the blood of the Chi.
But a legend is a legend. After all, who would be able to find traces of the Chi today?
What happened after that?

After that... in order to seal the corpse of the Chi and prevent it from endangering the world again, water was used to seal its corpse, and treasures were used to pin it in the center of the vault...
Hmm, the rest of it is illegible.
Does the Chi's corpse still exist?
I'm afraid that other than Rex Lapis, no one else knows the answer to that question.
So, young one, do you think that the things recorded on these three fragments are true?
Well, it's not a bad thing for a young person to bumble around a bit.
But if you really want to pursue your search according to the content of these fragments, then I say that the place you're looking for must have something to do with <color=#00E1FFFF>water</color>.
Not only that, but it must also be <color=#00E1FFFF>water</color> whose <color=#00E1FFFF>entrance</color> can be blocked.
Is it... a waterfall?
Let me think... Come to think of it, there is a sizable waterfall northwest of Qingce Village. I wonder if it has something to do with that vault...
Well, that's all I know. As for the rest, you'll have to mull it over yourself.
Is it a pool...?
Vaults... Treasure!
Haha, young one... you can't resist the thought of treasure, can you?
So, do you think that the things recorded on these three fragments are true?
You're back. So, did you find anything?
Not a thing.
Hahaha. It's alright, not to worry, there is nothing wrong with a bit of extra running around while you're young enough to handle it.
Here, these are for you. You've been out and about all day. Go buy something nice to eat, and rest your legs a bit.
So there was nothing inside... That's good, that's good...
We found a whole bunch of Treasure Hoarders outside.
Treasure Hoarders? Did you chase them off?
Those low-down, no-good crooks, always skulking about. They're so annoying. It's high time someone taught them a lesson.
And there was... nothing inside? Hahaha, no matter, no matter at all. there is nothing wrong with a bit of extra running around while you're young enough to handle it.
Here, these are for you. You've been out and about all day. Go buy something nice to eat, and rest your legs a bit.
So there was nothing inside... That's good, that's good...
Wow... Paimon can't make any sense of this at all.
Paimon can't tell if it's supposed to be a drawing, or writing, or... some other kind of thing.
Maybe the locals will have an idea.
Let's ask around in Qingce Village.
That makes three fragments we've found. And it looks like they match up...
So we just need to put them together, and... Nope. Still makes no sense to Paimon.
Guess we do need to ask the locals after all, huh...
...So that's it? Aw, but what about our monster corpse? And our treasure?
Surely a place this big can't be completely empty? And think of all the effort we've put into this...
Hmm... Shall we give it another once-over, just to be sure?
The Chi remains a shadow that haunts us. To think that someone would have designs on its corpse!
...Well, I can only hope that it's just that bunch of two-bit crooks. But if there truly is something down there...
...Ah, Geo Lord, protect us...
Hello, and welcome to Qingce Village.
How do you do?
You found a hidden chamber behind a waterfall?
What did you find inside?
Nothing special...
Nothing special, you say... That's good, that's good... best there be nothing special...
Haha, look at you two, covered in dust from head to toe... I'm sure you two had quite the unpleasant adventure in there too.
Here, take these. Go buy something nice to eat, and rest your legs a bit.
Um, we didn't do that much...
That's right, Granny, we didn't do anything at all!
Oh, listen to yourselves. Didn't you help us chase those Treasure Hoarders away from our village?
Allow me to give these to you as a token of appreciation, on behalf of everyone in Qingce Village.
We don't take payment if the work's not done...
We found a whole bunch of Treasure Hoarders outside.
Treasure Hoarders? Did you chase them off?
Those low-down, no-good crooks, always skulking about. They're so annoying. It's high time someone taught them a lesson.
So there was nothing special inside, you say? That's good, that's good... best there be nothing special...
Huh, so that's it? But we found nothing...
Let have another look, just to be sure. We've come this far... we gotta have something to show for it!
Those Treasure Hoarders look real scary. Paimon remembers that Qingce Village is nearby...
Let's go there, find someone and tell them about this. It's best that they be on guard.
We won't let these bad guys get their way!
These three lines are so hard to read... But they did mention that "three Chi Trees were used to subdue it..."
Chi Trees... Um, are they referring to <color=#00E1FFFF>some sort of tree</color>?
Let's look around, and look out for <color=#00E1FFFF>trees</color>. Who knows, we might find some clues!
So after all that running around, we still didn't find anything.
The Chi, the treasure, it's all just a legend!
Still, it's weird. Why did the village chief granny seem so happy about that?
The people of Qingce are really friendly. Hehe, guess we didn't come all this way for nothing.
Still, don't you feel like that granny was too happy about all this?
How can Paimon put this... Is kicking the Treasure Hoarders out something to be that happy about?
Take a look at this fragment?
Fragment? What fragment, is it from some toy that was broken?
I have never encountered a fragment of this kind before.
Perhaps you should ask the village chief. Perhaps she might know something.
Can you read this fragment?
A fragment? Hmm... No, I can't read it.
As a matter of fact, I've never seen one in my life.
You should go ask Granny Ruoxin, she might know something about it.
Know anything about this fragment?
A fragment? Let me see... I'm sorry, I've never seen anything like this.
But I think Granny Ruoxin might know. You should go ask her.
Excuse me, know anything about fragments?
Fragments? Mm... I don't know.
You should go ask Granny Ruoxin, she might know.
Look at this fragment!
Ah! You scared me! ...What fragment?
What is it? ...You don't know? Go ask Granny Ruoxin, she knows everything.
What do you make of this fragment?
A fragment? Uh...
Lemme see... Wow. I have no idea. I've never seen one of these before.
Why don't you go ask Granny Ruoxin?
I have this fragment...
A fragment, you say? Show me.
This writing... or maybe it's not writing at all. I can't read it, anyway.
Ask the village chief, she's gotta know something.
...This is something I never expected to see.
Well, if it's what fate has decreed...
Remind me about the fragments?
Forgotten already? Well, I do have a habit of rambling on and on I suppose...
If you're looking for fragments connected to the great war, you may have more luck searching in <color=#00E1FFFF>high-altitude</color> places.
Also, you should head <color=#00E1FFFF>west</color> and take a close look nearby the <color=#00E1FFFF>Geo Statues</color>.
Finally, it can't hurt to check the <color=#00E1FFFF>ruins</color> in this area.
What makes you so sure?
Hahaha... I never said I was sure, now, did I?
Let's just say that at my age, you sometimes find yourself remembering things that most people have forgotten.
When I was a child, everybody knew the tale of the Geo Lord suppressing the Chi.
But some people would say that even the Geo Lord himself couldn't wipe out the Chi completely, and so Geo Statues were used to press it down, slowly crushing it to death over time.
Haha. But of course, it's just an old story. If there was really a chance the Chi is still alive, we would hardly feel safe living here in Qingce Village.
